objects.name: Chipkin Example B-ACCR
objects.note: the device itself; the instance is configurable with --deviceID and the Object_Name with --deviceName (both at start-up; the heading shows the defaults). The stack rows are device-wide facts only the stack knows - the protocol version and revision it implements, the services and object types it was configured with, the live object list and address-binding table, and Database_Revision, which the stack starts at 0 and increments for each object added at start-up: it reads 6 (the Device, Analog Input 1, Binary Input 1, Multi-state Input 1, Credential Data Input 1 and Network Port 1) and stays 6, because nothing creates, deletes or renames an object afterwards (a card presentation or an Out_Of_Service write changes a value, not the object database). The accepted rows are the stack's configured defaults for APDU limits, segmentation and system status; an application that answered them from its own constants could contradict the stack, so this example does not

objects.name: Bronze
objects.note: REAL, degrees Celsius; starts at 21.5; Present_Value COV-subscribable (F-COV canonical example). COV_Increment 1.0 (required: the object supports COV reporting, cl. 12.2.16)

objects.name: Flax
objects.note: Present_Value is BACnetAuthenticationFactor (a 4-byte simple-number32 card ID, served via the OctetString callback; the stack always reports Format-Type 0 = UNDEFINED and Format-Class 0, so every read means "no current authentication factor" (cl. 12.36.4) - a stack gap that makes this a Blocked Example, see README.md); Supported_Formats is served via RegisterCallbackGetPropertyAuthenticationFactorFormat, Update_Time via the Time callback, which the stack wraps into a BACnetTimeStamp. Update_Time - NOT Present_Value - is the COV-subscribable property for this object type (135-2024 Table 13-1; F-COV canonical example, see TUTORIAL.md); the notification payload still carries Present_Value. The up/down keys simulate a new card presentation

objects.name: Vermilion
objects.note: BACnet/IP; Network_Type and Protocol_Level are set from BACnetStack_AddNetworkPortObject()'s arguments (IPv4, BACnet Application) at start-up, not a GetProperty callback like the object's other app-served rows; Changes_Pending is likewise computed and answered natively by the stack's Network Port object. Reliability has no fault condition this example detects, so it is accepted at the generic default (normal)
